title: Proportion decision card
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Enlargement and similarity; ratio and proportion; rates
source: Seeded from mathematics/y9 lesson 65 (Proportion decision card (printable, in the pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 65: Direct, inverse or neither? Proportion problem solving. To understand how to decide whether a situation is direct proportion, inverse proportion or neither, and choose the right method

questions.q: 5 sheets of paper weigh 25 g. How much do 120 sheets weigh?
questions.model: More sheets, more weight: direct. One sheet: 25 ÷ 5 = 5 g; 120 × 5 = 600 g.

questions.q: A pipe fills a pool in 9 hours. How long do three identical pipes take?
A runner runs 100 m in 15 s. A pupil says 1000 m takes 150 s. Is that realistic?
questions.a: No: runners slow down over longer distances; 150 s is only an estimate from a direct model.

questions.q: Decide direct, inverse or neither, then solve: (a) 8 m of rope weighs 2.4 kg: how much does 15 m weigh? (b) 6 printers print a batch of reports in 45 minutes: how long for 9 printers? (c) 12 boxes of dates fill 3 shelves: how many shelves for 20 boxes? (d) 4 machines make 900 bars in 6 hours: how many bars do 6 machines make in 5 hours?
questions.a: (a) direct: 4.5 kg (b) inverse: 30 minutes (c) direct: 5 shelves (d) 1125 bars
questions.model: (a) More rope, more weight: direct. 1 m weighs 2.4 ÷ 8 = 0.3 kg; 15 m weighs 15 × 0.3 = 4.5 kg. (d) One machine makes 900 ÷ 4 ÷ 6 = 37.5 bars an hour; 6 × 5 × 37.5 = 1125.

questions.q: A taxi charges £3 plus £2 a mile. Explain why the cost is not directly proportional to the miles, and find the cost of 7 miles.
questions.a: £17; the £3 fixed charge means 0 miles does not cost £0, so the graph misses the origin.

questions.q: 8 people take 6 days to harvest an olive grove. After 2 days, 4 more people join. How many days does the harvest take in total?
questions.a: 48 person-days; 16 done, 32 left for 12 people = 2⅔ days; total 4⅔ days

questions.q: Speed and time for a fixed distance are:
A taxi at £3 plus £2 a mile: proportional?
Big question: how do you decide which kind of proportion a problem uses?
questions.a: Ask whether more of one gives more or less of the other, then check for a constant ratio (direct) or product (inverse); if neither, it is not proportion.
